name: Straight-Front Corset
summary: The long, straight-busk corset of the Edwardian years. It presses the stomach flat, throws the hip back and the bust forward, and gives the S-curve of the 1900 silhouette.

philosophy.core_thesis: A corset that is cut straight in front and low on the bust is healthier and gives the new S-shaped line of 1900.
design_principles: Cut the front busk long and straight, 35 to 45 cm, so that the stomach lies flat.
Cut the top edge low at the bust, so that the bust is free and sits forward.
Cut the back to curve in at the waist and out at the hip, to push the hip back.
Reduce the pressure on the stomach, and put the hold on the hip and the back.
Make the body of coutil or strong cotton, with spring steel in the busk and the bones.
Add four suspenders to the lower edge, for the stockings.
Trim the top with machine lace and a narrow ribbon.
anti_patterns: A short corset that curves in at the stomach
A high, full bust held up by the bone
A soft bandeau bra with no waist
A round hourglass with no forward tilt

silhouette.shape: An S-curve: a full bust forward, a small waist, and a hip pushed back, with a flat, long front.
silhouette.line: A long line from the bust to the thigh; the front is straight and the back curves in.
silhouette.fit: Firm on the waist and the hip, low and loose on the bust; the busk guides the stomach flat.
silhouette.proportion: Busk 35 to 45 cm; waist 55 to 60 cm; the corset reaches 10 to 15 cm below the waist at the front.
rules: Run the front busk straight from the bust to the groin.
Cut the top edge at or below the bust line.
Set a steel strip at each side of the back lacing.
Hang four suspenders from the lower edge.
Cover the top with a corset cover of cotton and lace.

fabrics.rule: Use coutil for the body and spring steel for the busk; add satin or silk for show, with elastic webbing in the suspenders.

methods: long panels cut to a graded pattern
straight busk of two spring-steel plates
metal eyelets in a laced back
lace and ribbon at the top edge
construction.closures: A long busk of studs and loops at the front, with a cord laced through metal eyelets at the back.
construction.details: Suspenders of elastic with a metal clip, a ribbon at the top, a small lace flounce, and a stay-bone at each hip.

surface.pattern: Plain white or pale colour; fine broderie, small flowers or a stripe on a corset for show.
surface.gloss: Coutil at 3–8 GU; satin and taffeta at 30–60 GU.
surface.wear: The lower edge creases from sitting, and the busk bends after a year of daily use.

palette.strategy: White, pale pink and pale blue, with black for mourning; the line, not the colour, is the point.

processes: panels sewn on a machine in a factory
metal eyelets set by a machine
making.scale: Made in a factory in standard sizes in Paris, London and the United States; a fitted corset was also made to measure by a corsetière.
making.signs: It has a long straight busk, a low bust line and a back that curves out at the hip. It also has suspenders at the hem and a trade stamp on the inside.

pieces.form: Long straight-busk corset in coutil, low at the bust
Corset in satin with a lace top and a ribbon
Cotton corset cover with a lace edge
Silk taffeta petticoat with a flounce at the hem
Knitted silk stockings held by the corset suspenders

canonical_works.work: Peach silk corset with metal bones, hooks and studs

evidence.title: Peach silk corset with metal bones, about 1910

emotion.target_response: A sense of upright poise: a long line, a forward bust and a flat front that carries the lace and the tailored skirt.

use_cases: a museum label or object study
avoid_when: the brief wants a soft bra of the 1920s
the brief wants the older steel-busk hourglass

modifiers.how: Shorten the busk, curve in at the stomach, add gussets, and keep the coutil and the steel.
Remove the bone and the busk, and flatten the bust with a plain band of silk or cotton.

ornament_level.note: The day corset is plain; a corset for show carries lace and ribbon.
